title: Elastic Request Triage & Response Thinning for Overload Protection
creator: Priya Desai
description: Background: Regional traffic spikes and cross-region failovers periodically push serving fleets above headroom. Existing hard drops (rejecting requests) and blunt truncation cause disproportionate customer impact and noisy SLO violations. Goal: Implement an elastic triage pipeline that admits high-value requests, gracefully thins responses where acceptable, and provides deterministic, observable behavior during overloads so SREs and product owners can reason about impact. Scope: runtime admission hint layer + lightweight response-thinning transformations + operator controls and dashboards. Out of scope: model re-training, billing changes, long-lived batch backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Triage policy applies per-tenant and per-route with deterministic priority buckets
Under 2x baseline QPS spike the system keeps P95 latency within SLO for top-tier tenants while trimming non-essential tokens for lower tiers
Response thinning APIs expose original/trimmed token counts and reason codes in trace/span metadata
Rollout flag allows gradual enablement by region and tenant and can be disabled centrally with immediate effect
Dashboards show real-time admitted vs rejected vs thinned counts and estimated token-cost savings
design_notes: We propose a two-stage approach: (1) Admission classifier: lightweight policy service that annotates requests with an admission decision — accept, deferred (queue), thin, or reject — based on token budget, tenant SLA tier, and current shard headroom. This lives in the front proxy before heavy deserialization. (2) Thinning transformations: modular transformers that can (a) apply prefix-preservation and suffix-truncation heuristics, (b) downgrade decoding temperature or max_tokens, or (c) apply structured field elision for JSON outputs. Trade-offs: Doing complex thinning in the proxy increases latency; we keep policy decision extremely cheap (<500us) and defer heavier mutate ops to the runtime worker where KV cache is available. Determinism: decisions are based on deterministic tenant fingerprints and current headroom to reduce flapping during rollouts. We avoid ML scoring for now to reduce instability at scale.
implementation_plan: 1. Policy proto & API: define admission proto with decision enum and reason codes (ENG-312345-01)
2. Proxy hook: call policy service with request metadata; apply decision annotation (ENG-312345-02)
3. Runtime integration: runtime reads decision annotation and applies thinning transformer pipeline (ENG-312345-03)
4. Operator controls: console flags, tenant overrides, and kill-switch (ENG-312345-04)
5. Observability: add metrics/counters, traces, and dashboard panels (ENG-312345-05)
6. E2E tests + chaos harness: simulate region failover and sudden QPS ramps (ENG-312345-06)
7. Gradual rollout: canary small subset of tenants, expand by region, monitor SLOs
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy logic and decision encoding
Integration test with runtime transformer and KV cache present
Load tests: 1.5x, 2x, 3x baseline QPS with mixed tenant mix and downstream latency variance
Chaos test: simulate pod churn + region blackout to validate deterministic fallback behavior
Canary verification checks: compare quality metrics (per-prompt acceptance, completion rate, token delta) against baseline
monitoring_and_dashboard: SLOs: P95 latency and error rate by tier with flag-enabled overlay
Dashboard: realtime tile for admitted/thinned/rejected ratios and per-tenant noisy neighbor alarms
Alert: sustained rejected_rate > 1% for P0 tenants or admitted_latency breach for >10 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature gated implementation in staging; run synthetic traffic tests
Phase 1: enable for internal tenants only (sec-team, infra) for 48h
Phase 2: canary 5% of low-risk external tenants in us-west, monitor 72h
Phase 3: expand to all tenants in us-west and replicate to us-east with 24h observation
Phase 4: global enablement with tenant opt-outs and documented runbook
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Desai: Scoped initial spike-mitigation work. SRE reported recurring mid-day regional bursts causing repeated fallbacks. Proposing admission + thinning rather than immediate rejects.
2026-03-03 Evan Li: Prototype for policy proto written (ENG-312345-01). Measured RPC call adds ~320us median in staging; acceptable but we'll optimize with in-proxy batching if needed.
2026-03-05 Design review (Miguel Torres): Recommended adding structured-elision strategy to preserve key JSON fields for tooling customers. Suggested adding reason codes for finer telemetry.
2026-03-07 QA (Aisha Khan): Load tests at 2x baseline show 40% token savings for mid-tier when thinning enabled; need to tune heuristics to avoid quality cliffs on question-answer prompts.

2026-03-09 SRE note (Jian Wu): Dependency on shard headroom API is a blocker—current headroom signals are 3s stale for large fleets. Proposal: switch to local shard reservoir estimate while we fix headroom pipeline (tracked separately).
